WARNING!!!!!!!!! SPOILERS AHEAD, MAJOR MASSIVE SPOILERS!!!!!!!!!! TURN BACK NOW IF YOU HAVEN'T SEEN IT!!!!!!!

I know I can't be the only one who thought it was absolutely crap. It looked like what would happen if Universal Studios approached Sifee (SyFy...I refuse to pronounce that dumbass spelling correctly) and said "pull literally anything out of your ass and we will fund the shit out of it". The CG was worse than the original JP, which has a solid excuse in the fact that it was damn good CG for it's time. The characters were shit and unfleshed out as well. For instance:

Dr. Ian Malcolm - A mathematician who specializes in chaos theory. This is told within the first JP movie, and let's you know who and what he is. He has his laugh, and dry and somewhat sarcastic humor which are memorable (it also helps that Jeff Goldblum is a great actor).

Alan Grant - A paleontologist with a passion for discovery and a slightly cynical approach to things.

Ellie Sattler - A high energy, beautiful but not sexualized paleobotanist. She's bright, cheerful, and the perfect balance to Alans cynical character.

These are our main characters that we get to follow throughout the movie (along with the kids, who also were well written characters). I remember their names, their personalities, their jobs, etc. The story is well written, and assuming we could bring back the "Din-uh-sawers", it's a believable SHTF scenario.

Now let's take a look at the newer movie. I'm going to go into greater detail with JW because I assume we all know about the original(s).

Chris Pratt - No fucking idea what his name was. His character was the only one with any real personality, and I personally credit that to the fact that Pratt is a good up-and-coming actor. That said, his character, though useful, was unnecessary. What did he do? I assume he cared for the (inexplicably) super locked down raptors...that apparently never left their stocks. Secondary point: Why the hell did they even have raptors since they apparently were so scared of them/understood their high level of intelligence so well that they locked them down? Since they have them locked down and basically useless, why the fuck did they put cameras and shit on them?

Claire Dearing - Once again, the character and ergo the name don't stick out because they are hollow. Owner? No, she got taken over...I'll guess manager or equivalent because it sure as fuck wasn't very well explained. Might have been mentioned in passing, or written on a window that I didn't care to look at.

Vincent D'Onofrio?! - The fuck? What is he...ok, so he's, I guess, JW security. And he sucks gargantuan unprofessional ass at his job. Thankfully, he died like a bitch.

The Parents - Who the fuck are they? Why teh hell are they sending their kids to such a place alone? Fuck it.

The Kids - Fuck names, I'm not even paying attention anymore. Which is sad, because after Pratt, they gave the second best performances for the entire movie - and they weren't terribly great at that.

Enough with the actors, let's dive into the story.

Original: Rich bastard gets funding to clone dinosaurs - the best way to keep such a huge undertaking profitable is to bring in the public interest - the best way to do that is a theme park-slash-zoo. (People love theme parks, and you know that if htey were able to bring back dinos that's what would happen.) So once they have things going, they need advice and opinions from people who studied the creatures bones and habitats. Enter Grant and Sattler, and we will bring in a mathematician (for statistical purposes, I suppose?). Cynical dude says shits making him uneasy, chaos theorist predicts...chaos, and the bubbly one says jeez guys, lol. SHTF, everyone runs for their lives and gets the fuck off the island. Simple, believable, and allows for decent story, characters, and timing of events. It allows for memorable characters (even if their names were not as memorable as the core group). Fat guy who betrays employer and has an awesome exit, snarky computer dude with smart remarks, stereotypical aussie game warden with a legendary exit, etc.

Jurassic World: A pair of nobodies send their kids to visit Mrs. Nobodys sister who ignores them. Some Dude In A Vest enters the cage of a super mutant (like a dumbass), the super mutant happens to still be there (GASP) and they run like hell but they done fucked up like half an hour into the movie. Everyone runs around in a retarded panic, but not panicky enough considering a carnivorous 20 foot tall beast is rampaging around. The kids decide to break the rules and get attacked, and somehow they didn't care to develop that branch of the story. Sister Nobody shits her panties but not too badly, Man In A Vest heads out and she decides to follow. Surprise surprise, the murder monster they created to be a scary badass is a scary badass murder monster, cause it's killing god damn everything. Security Guy decides to unleash the fucking raptors to hunt the murder monster...and things TOTALLY GO ACCORDING TO PLAN BECAUSE EVERYONE LEARNED THE LESSON ABOUT RAPTORS THAT WAS LAID OUT SOME 20 YEARS PRIOR. No not really, the raptors decide they like the murder monster. Some more stuff happens(I'm gonna skip a lot, it's all kinda unimportant fluff anyway), the murder monster finds it's way to the buffet, and the Grand Plan is to FUCKING LET THE T-REX OUT OF IT'S ENCLOSURE. WHAT THE SHIT. But it's ok, our genetic super mutant murder monster, which is a mix of a brutal massive T-Rex and the agile and super smart Velociraptor, is a pussy compared to a vanilla Rex(I have no idea). Then Sister Nobody kisses The Vest and everyone is happy and stuff.

What. The. Fuck. I left out some details, and I am in fact biased because the original movie (Jurassic Park) came out when I was little. But I pretty much never out right hate remakes/reboots/reinvigorations/sequels/pre-quels/whatever the fuck type of movie this was supposed to be. This movie however, was immediately such a steamer that I had to make a post. The opening scene was already a major let down, and it literally only got worse as the movie progressed.

Anyhoo, this has gotten way to long.

Thoughts?

Let's not forget the original movie was based on the actual Michael Crichton novel, so it not surprising that it's got better written characters and plot. Yes, the original is a better movie but I enjoyed Jurassic World.

I really liked the fact that's choke full of 90's nostalgia (intentional or not). Like the whole plot point about greedy corporations, reloading only for dramatic effect, impossible physics, not to mention high heels you can run away from dinosaurs in.

It's also chock full of plot holes, unacceptably weak characters, and and completely ridiculous plot. A movie doesn't need to be based on a book to be good (The Book of Eli, Transcendence, Interstellar, Fury). Each of these had believable, strong characters that felt either relateable, believable, or both (short fanboy segment: Pitt was incredible in Fury, there was basically NONE of his known style in the character).

My stance is this: There is absolutely a place for a movie like Jurassic World, but the footsteps of a good and established trilogy is not the place. I suppose since they changed the name (World instead of Park) I shouldn't bash it so hard, but damn them they had to put a location from the original in it! An old vine and moss covered building that ended up having the original jeeps in it!

I'm not saying you're wrong but let's face it, the other 2 sequels didn't live up to the original either. Based on that fact alone, I didn't have high expectations for JW. Could they have done things better? Absolutely. I wanted to see more accurate science, better pacing to build up suspense, plot points that made sense.

I don't think this, or the other sequels, is a movie you can go in expecting more of Jurassic Park because it's never going to be recreated. It's a simple, fun summer movie with dinosaurs and it doesn't pretend to be more than that.

BTW, before you blow an artery over this, the way they left Dr. Wu's plot point hanging means there will be a JW2, guaranteed.

I never really cared about any characters other than Dr. Wu(who seemed to be the only person who knew anything on that island). It equally doesn't make sense that Pratt can talk to a raptor in English and have it understand every word and decide to turn on its new leader, but I don't care. The plot and story was crap and heavy-handed. Why should I care that the kids parents are getting a divorce? They also were trying so hard to make the older kid such a piece of shit in the beginning that it was painfully obvious after 10 min that he's going to do a 180 and protect his brother. Same with Redheaded Heels(Claire, apparently).

Overall, it was an ok movie. Good action scenes but bad storytelling. Not one I want to bother seeing again.
